result.summary: The page structure is generally sound, but the promo banner text is nearly illegible due to white-on-light-green contrast, and several carousel/card elements are clipped or inconsistently styled.

issues.description: The green promo banner uses white text ('3 free deliveries for you' and the code/min-order line) on a very light mint background, giving very low contrast and making the offer details hard to read.
issues.suggestion: Use a dark green or near-black text color on the light background (or darken the banner background) so text meets at least 4.5:1 contrast.

issues.description: The third restaurant card in 'Fastest near you' is hard-clipped by the viewport edge — the name reads 'Trattoria Piccol' and the delivery price is cut mid-line, with no visible affordance that the row scrolls.
issues.suggestion: Add consistent horizontal padding/peek for the carousel, truncate long titles with an ellipsis, and add a scroll indicator or partial-card peek so the row is clearly swipeable.

issues.description: Favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently: the Tokumaru Ramen card has a white circular button while the pizza card below has a dark/transparent circular button, so the same control looks like two different states.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the favorite button background and icon color across all cards, and use fill state only to indicate saved/unsaved.

issues.description: The category filter chip row is cut off at the right edge with only a sliver of the next chip visible, which reads as a rendering glitch rather than a scrollable list.
issues.suggestion: Align chip row padding with the page gutter and show a clear partial chip or fade/gradient edge to signal scrollability.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card is cut off by the fixed bottom navigation bar with no bottom spacing, so its title/metadata are hidden behind the nav.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding to the scroll container equal to the nav bar height so the last card can fully scroll into view.

issues.description: Restaurant card images appear as heavily blurred/generic illustrations with strong vignettes, making dishes hard to identify and looking like low-quality placeholders.
issues.suggestion: Replace with sharp, properly cropped photography and reduce the dark overlay so only the badge areas are darkened for legibility.
